title: Chicken and Wild Rice Bake with Squash-Sage Gravy
description: Cooked wild rice and tender chicken bake under a lid in a roux-thickened butternut and sage gravy.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: butternut squash neck
ingredients.note: Peel and cut into small dice.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

ingredients.name: plain cooked wild rice
ingredients.note: Use fully cooked, tender, unsalted wild rice. Measure after cooking.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the Samsung oven to 350°F on conventional Bake with the rack in the middle.

steps.title: Soften the squash
steps.text: Simmer {squash} and {sage} in {broth} in the covered HexClad for 10–15 minutes until the squash crushes easily with a spoon.

steps.title: Puree the squash
steps.text: Blend the squash and all its cooking liquid in a deep heatproof jug until smooth.

steps.title: Make a pale roux
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the emptied HexClad over medium-low heat. Whisk in {flour} for 2 minutes until the paste smells lightly toasted.

steps.title: Whisk the gravy
steps.text: Gradually whisk the squash puree and {milk} into the roux. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Assemble the casserole
steps.text: Spread {rice} in the casserole and stir in half the hot gravy. Cut {chicken} into 3/4-inch pieces and arrange over the rice. Cover with the remaining gravy and fit the lid.

steps.title: Bake covered
steps.text: Bake for 20–32 minutes, checking from 18 minutes, until the thickest chicken pieces reach 175°F and the rice at the center reaches at least 165°F.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Rest covered for 3 minutes. Spoon the chicken and wild rice into shallow bowls and ladle gravy from the dish over each serving.

notes: Sauce yield: About 3 cups of gravy for four before baking. The cooked rice takes up some liquid and leaves roughly 1/2 cup of gravy per portion. Make ahead: Cook the wild rice until tender the day before and chill promptly. Bring the squash gravy to a simmer before assembling the casserole. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The cooked rice and puree reheat well when frozen under the gravy for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: Spoon one portion and its sauce into a small covered oven-safe dish. Warm at 325°F on conventional Bake, checking after 15 minutes, until the coldest center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. For dairy-free gravy, use avocado oil for the butter and unsweetened oat milk for the skim milk. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 341 kcal, 33.7 g protein, 24.6 g total carbohydrate, 11.9 g fat, 2.4 g fiber, 174 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth.
